Induction gemcitabine plus cisplatin followed by concurrent chemoradiotherapy significantly improves recurrence-free and overall survival in locoregionally advanced nasopharyngeal carcinoma.

First-line toripalimab or camrelizumab PD-1 inhibitors combined with gemcitabine and cisplatin significantly improve progression-free and overall survival in advanced metastatic nasopharyngeal carcinoma.
Adenoid cystic carcinoma ACC of salivary glands is characterized by the hallmark MYB-NFIB gene fusion, indolent growth, distinctive perineural invasion, and late pulmonary metastases.
mustKnow.source: WHO Head and Neck Tumours / DeVita 12e Ch. 29

mustKnow.fact: Mucoepidermoid carcinoma of the salivary glands is defined by the t(11;19) translocation creating the CRTC1-MAML2 fusion oncogene, correlating with lower histological grade and favourable prognosis.

Salivary duct carcinoma is an aggressive, high-grade malignancy histologically resembling invasive mammary ductal carcinoma, exhibiting strong androgen receptor positivity and frequent HER2 amplification.
Targeted anti-androgen therapy bicalutamide or enzalutamide and anti-HER2 therapies trastuzumab and T-DM1 demonstrate meaningful clinical responses in advanced salivary duct carcinomas.

topics.title: Thyroid cancer
topics.book: DeVita 12e Ch. 54 (Thyroid Tumors and Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia)

mustKnow.fact: Papillary thyroid carcinoma PTC is the most common endocrine malignancy, characterized cytologically by ground-glass Orphan Annie nuclei, nuclear pseudoinclusions, and psammoma bodies.
BRAF V600E point mutations occur in approximately 60% of papillary thyroid carcinomas, associated with aggressive clinicopathological features and loss of radioiodine avidity.
Lenvatinib multi-targeted TKI significantly improves progression-free survival and objective response rate in radioactive iodine-refractory differentiated thyroid cancer in the SELECT trial.
Sorafenib multi-kinase inhibitor prolongs progression-free survival in radioactive iodine-refractory advanced differentiated thyroid carcinoma based on the randomized DECISION trial.
Medullary thyroid carcinoma MTC arises from calcitonin-secreting parafollicular C cells, strongly driven by germline or somatic activating RET proto-oncogene mutations.
Highly selective RET inhibitors selpercatinib and pralsetinib demonstrate profound, durable antitumor activity in advanced RET-mutant medullary and RET-fusion thyroid carcinomas in LIBRETTO-001.
Anaplastic thyroid carcinoma ATC is an undifferentiated, highly lethal malignancy; BRAF V600E-mutant ATC responds rapidly to combination dabrafenib and trametinib targeted therapy.
mustKnow.source: Subbiah et al. (JCO) / ATA ATC Guidelines

mustKnow.fact: Serum thyroglobulin Tg measured under TSH stimulation is the primary surveillance biomarker for identifying persistent or recurrent disease after thyroidectomy and radioiodine remnant ablation.

topics.title: Central nervous system tumours
topics.book: DeVita 12e Ch. 64 (Neoplasms of the Central Nervous System)

mustKnow.fact: WHO CNS5 classification establishes that glioblastoma is defined by IDH-wildtype status plus microvascular proliferation, necrosis, or molecular features like TERT promoter mutation or EGFR amplification.
MGMT promoter methylation silences DNA repair O6-methylguanine-DNA methyltransferase, predicting profound benefit and prolonged survival from temozolomide chemotherapy in glioblastoma.
The Stupp protocol combining maximal safe surgical resection with radiotherapy 60 Gy and concurrent daily temozolomide followed by 6 cycles of adjuvant temozolomide is standard for glioblastoma.

Tumour treating fields TTFields delivering low-intensity alternating electrical fields to the scalp combined with maintenance temozolomide significantly improves overall survival in glioblastoma in EF-14.
Oligodendrogliomas are defined by IDH mutation and complete, unbalanced whole-arm 1p and 19q chromosomal co-deletion, predicting high chemosensitivity to PCV procarbazine, lomustine, vincristine.
Vorasidenib is a brain-penetrant dual inhibitor of mutant IDH1 and IDH2, significantly prolonging progression-free survival in residual or recurrent grade 2 IDH-mutant glioma in INDIGO.
Medulloblastoma is divided into 4 molecular subgroups: WNT associated with CTNNB1 mutations and excellent prognosis, SHH, Group 3 with MYC amplification, and Group 4.
Primary CNS lymphoma PCNSL is predominantly diffuse large B-cell lymphoma; induction with high-dose methotrexate-based regimens like MATRix provides the foundation for curative therapy.

topics.title: Melanoma
topics.book: DeVita 12e Ch. 63 (Cutaneous and Noncutaneous Melanoma)

mustKnow.fact: Activating BRAF V600 mutations V600E and V600K occur in approximately 40% to 50% of cutaneous melanomas, driving constitutive oncogenic MAPK pathway signaling.
Dual targeted therapy combining BRAF and MEK inhibitors dabrafenib plus trametinib or encorafenib plus binimetinib produces rapid objective response rates exceeding 65% in BRAF-mutant melanoma.
Nivolumab plus ipilimumab dual checkpoint blockade established durable 5-year overall survival exceeding 50% in advanced melanoma in CheckMate 067.
Nivolumab combined with relatlimab anti-LAG-3 significantly improves progression-free survival compared to nivolumab monotherapy in untreated metastatic melanoma in RELATIVITY-047.
Adjuvant anti-PD-1 monotherapy with pembrolizumab or nivolumab for 1 year significantly prolongs recurrence-free survival in resected stage IIB, IIC, and III melanoma.
Neoadjuvant dual immunotherapy with ipilimumab plus nivolumab induces high pathological complete response rates in macroscopic stage III melanoma in the NADINA trial.
Tebentafusp is a bispecific gp100 peptide-HLA-A*02:01-directed T-cell receptor therapeutic improving overall survival in HLA-A*02:01-positive metastatic uveal melanoma.
Sentinel lymph node biopsy SLNB is the standard staging procedure for cutaneous melanomas with Breslow thickness 0.8 mm or greater or thinner lesions with ulceration.

topics.title: Non-melanoma skin cancers
topics.book: DeVita 12e Ch. 62 (Non-Melanoma Skin Cancers and Merkel Cell Carcinoma)

mustKnow.fact: Basal cell carcinoma BCC is the most common human cancer, driven by aberrant constitutive activation of the Hedgehog signaling pathway through PTCH1 loss-of-function or SMO activating mutations.
Oral Hedgehog pathway inhibitors vismodegib and sonidegib bind smoothened SMO to achieve high objective response rates in locally advanced or metastatic basal cell carcinoma.
Cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma cSCC carries high ultraviolet radiation mutational burden, responding robustly to anti-PD-1 monoclonal antibodies cemiplimab and pembrolizumab.
Merkel cell carcinoma MCC is an aggressive cutaneous neuroendocrine carcinoma driven by Merkel cell polyomavirus MCPyV integration in 80% of European/US cases or chronic UV damage.
Avelumab anti-PD-L1 antibody induces rapid, durable objective responses in chemotherapy-refractory and treatment-naive metastatic Merkel cell carcinoma in the JAVELIN Merkel 200 trial.
Xeroderma pigmentosum XP is an autosomal recessive disorder caused by defective nucleotide excision repair NER, conferring a 10,000-fold increased risk of developing skin malignancies.
Gorlin syndrome nevoid basal cell carcinoma syndrome is caused by germline PTCH1 mutations, predisposing to dozens or hundreds of basal cell carcinomas, odontogenic keratocysts, and medulloblastomas.
Mohs micrographic surgery provides the highest cure rates for high-risk facial basal cell and squamous cell carcinomas by microscopically examining 100% of surgical margins intraoperatively.

topics.title: Soft tissue sarcomas
topics.book: DeVita 12e Ch. 60 (Soft Tissue Sarcomas)

mustKnow.fact: Well-differentiated and dedifferentiated liposarcomas are cytogenetically defined by supernumerary ring or giant chromosomes carrying pathognomonic 12q13-15 amplification containing MDM2 and CDK4.
mustKnow.source: WHO Soft Tissue Tumours / DeVita 12e Ch. 60

mustKnow.fact: Synovial sarcoma is driven by the pathognomonic reciprocal translocation t(X;18)(p11.2;q11.2), fusing SS18 with SSX1, SSX2, or SSX4.
First-line chemotherapy for advanced soft tissue sarcomas is doxorubicin monotherapy or combination doxorubicin plus ifosfamide, which maximizes objective response rate in chemosensitive subtypes.
Trabectedin binds the minor groove of DNA and modulates the tumour microenvironment, demonstrating efficacy in advanced pretreated liposarcomas and leiomyosarcomas.
Eribulin mesylate microtubule inhibitor significantly improves overall survival compared to dacarbazine in advanced or metastatic pretreated liposarcoma.
Pazopanib is an oral multi-targeted VEGFR/PDGFR kinase inhibitor approved for advanced non-adipocytic soft tissue sarcomas progressing after anthracycline chemotherapy in the PALETTE trial.

Desmoid tumours aggressive fibromatosis are locally infiltrative fibroblastic proliferations driven by CTNNB1 beta-catenin or APC mutations, managed with active surveillance, sorafenib, or nirogacestat.
Angiosarcoma is an aggressive vascular endothelial malignancy occurring de novo or secondary to prior radiotherapy Stewart-Treves syndrome or chronic lymphedema, responsive to weekly paclitaxel.

topics.title: Bone sarcomas
topics.book: DeVita 12e Ch. 61 (Sarcomas of Bone)

mustKnow.fact: Osteosarcoma is the most common primary malignant bone tumour, occurring predominantly in adolescents at the metaphysis of the distal femur and proximal tibia.
Classical radiographic appearance of osteosarcoma includes cortical destruction, soft tissue mass, sunburst periosteal reaction, and Codman triangle formed by subperiosteal new bone elevation.

Standard curative therapy for localized osteosarcoma is neoadjuvant and adjuvant MAP chemotherapy high-dose methotrexate with leucovorin rescue, doxorubicin, and cisplatin combined with limb-sparing surgical resection.
Pathological tumour necrosis of 90% or greater in the resected osteosarcoma specimen following neoadjuvant chemotherapy defines a good histological response and superior event-free survival.
Ewing sarcoma is a small round blue cell tumour of bone driven by the characteristic reciprocal translocation t(11;22)(q24;q12), generating the oncogenic EWSR1-FLI1 fusion transcript in 85% of cases.
Standard multi-agent chemotherapy for localized Ewing sarcoma consists of compressed interval dose-dense VDC/IE vincristine, doxorubicin, cyclophosphamide alternating with ifosfamide and etoposide.
Chondrosarcoma is an intrinsically chemoresistant and radioresistant cartilaginous malignancy, requiring complete en bloc wide surgical excision as the primary curative modality.
Giant cell tumour of bone is a locally aggressive osteolytic lesion characterized by RANKL overexpression by stromal cells, successfully treated with denosumab RANKL monoclonal antibody.

topics.title: Cancer of unknown primary
topics.book: DeVita 12e Ch. 75 (Cancer of Unknown Primary)

mustKnow.fact: Cancer of unknown primary CUP accounts for 2% to 5% of all cancer diagnoses, defined as biopsy-proven metastatic malignancy without an identifiable anatomical primary site after standardized workup.
Initial diagnostic immunohistochemical algorithm utilizes cytokeratin 7 CK7 and cytokeratin 20 CK20 staining patterns to narrow down likely anatomical origins.
Favourable CUP subsets comprise 15% to 20% of cases, demonstrating specific clinicopathological presentations that respond to site-directed curative-intent therapies.
Women presenting with isolated axillary lymph node adenocarcinoma are treated according to stage II breast cancer guidelines with axillary dissection, systemic therapy, and breast irradiation.

Women presenting with peritoneal carcinomatosis of papillary serous adenocarcinoma histology are managed identically to stage III epithelial ovarian carcinoma with cytoreduction and platinum chemotherapy.
Young men with midline mediastinal or retroperitoneal poorly differentiated carcinoma represent the extragonadal midline germ cell syndrome, curable with platinum-based BEP regimens.
Squamous cell carcinoma in cervical upper neck lymph nodes is evaluated with PET-CT, panendoscopy, and bilateral palatine and lingual tonsillectomy to identify occult HPV-driven primary tumours.
Unfavourable CUP subsets lacking actionable drivers are empirically treated with platinum-based doublets such as carboplatin plus paclitaxel or gemcitabine.

topics.title: HIV-associated malignancies
topics.book: DeVita 12e Ch. 77 (HIV-Associated and Immunodeficiency Malignancies)

mustKnow.fact: AIDS-defining malignancies include Kaposi sarcoma, non-Hodgkin lymphoma DLBCL, primary CNS lymphoma, Burkitt lymphoma, and invasive cervical cancer.

Kaposi sarcoma is caused by human herpesvirus 8 HHV-8 / KSHV, presenting with violaceous cutaneous, mucosal, or visceral spindle-cell lesions expressing CD31 and latency-associated nuclear antigen LANA.
First-line systemic therapy for advanced symptomatic visceral or cutaneous Kaposi sarcoma is liposomal doxorubicin combined with immediate combination antiretroviral therapy cART.
Primary effusion lymphoma is a rare, aggressive large B-cell lymphoma caused by HHV-8 coinfected with EBV, presenting as lymphomatous body-cavity effusions without discrete solid tumour masses.
Plasmablastic lymphoma is an aggressive B-cell neoplasm strongly linked to HIV and EBV, expressing plasma cell markers CD138 and MUM1 while lacking mature B-cell CD20 expression.
Standard curative chemotherapy regimens such as R-CHOP or dose-adjusted EPOCH can be safely delivered to HIV-associated diffuse large B-cell lymphomas alongside cART and G-CSF support.
Antiretroviral drug interactions must be actively monitored: ritonavir and cobicistat strongly inhibit CYP3A4, dramatically increasing toxic exposures of vincristine, taxanes, and kinase inhibitors.
HPV-associated anal squamous cell carcinoma incidence is markedly elevated in HIV-infected individuals, warranting digital anorectal examination and high-resolution anoscopy screening.

topics.title: Acute myeloid leukaemia
topics.book: DeVita 12e Ch. 70 (Acute Myeloid Leukemia)

mustKnow.fact: Diagnostic cutoff for acute myeloid leukaemia AML is 20% or more myeloblasts in bone marrow or blood, except when recurring genetics t(8;21), inv(16), or PML-RARA are present.
ELN 2022 risk stratification classifies AML into favourable RUNX1-RUNX1T1, CBFB-MYH11, NPM1 without FLT3-ITD, bZIP CEBPA; intermediate; and adverse adverse cytogenetics, TP53, ASXL1, RUNX1.
Standard intensive induction therapy 7+3 consists of continuous infusion cytarabine 100-200 mg/m2 for 7 days plus daunorubicin 60-90 mg/m2 or idarubicin for 3 days.
Midostaurin multi-kinase inhibitor added to 7+3 chemotherapy significantly improves overall and event-free survival in newly diagnosed FLT3-mutated AML in the RATIFY trial.
Gilteritinib is an oral selective FLT3 inhibitor significantly improving response and overall survival compared to salvage chemotherapy in relapsed or refractory FLT3-mutated AML in ADMIRAL.
Venetoclax BCL-2 inhibitor combined with azacitidine significantly improves complete remission rate and overall survival in older or intensive chemotherapy-ineligible AML in VIALE-A.

CPX-351 is a liposomal formulation of cytarabine and daunorubicin fixed at a synergistic 5:1 molar ratio, improving overall survival in therapy-related AML and AML with myelodysplasia-related changes.
Allogeneic haematopoietic stem cell transplantation in first complete remission CR1 is the standard consolidative treatment of choice for intermediate- and adverse-risk AML.

topics.title: Acute promyelocytic leukaemia
topics.book: DeVita 12e Ch. 70 (Acute Promyelocytic Leukemia)

mustKnow.fact: Acute promyelocytic leukaemia APL is defined by the balanced reciprocal translocation t(15;17)(q22;q12), creating the pathognomonic PML-RARA fusion oncoprotein.
The Spanish PETHEMA / Sanz risk score stratifies APL into low risk WBC 10 x 10^9/L or less and platelets over 40 x 10^9/L, intermediate risk, and high risk WBC over 10 x 10^9/L.
All-trans retinoic acid ATRA plus arsenic trioxide ATO combination therapy without cytotoxic chemotherapy achieves complete remission in 95% to 100% of non-high-risk APL in APL0406.

Differentiation syndrome retinoic acid syndrome presents with unexplained fever, weight gain, dyspnea, pulmonary infiltrates, and pleural/pericardial effusions, treated immediately with dexamethasone 10 mg twice daily.

Disseminated intravascular coagulation DIC with severe hypofibrinogenemia and elevated D-dimer is an oncologic emergency requiring aggressive platelet and cryoprecipitate replacement maintaining fibrinogen above 150 mg/dL.
Immediate administration of ATRA must never be delayed for cytogenetic or molecular confirmation when acute promyelocytic leukaemia is suspected clinically or morphologically.
High-risk APL WBC exceeding 10 x 10^9/L requires cytoreduction with an anthracycline or gemtuzumab ozogamicin added to ATRA and ATO to prevent fatal early differentiation and coagulopathy.
Arsenic trioxide ATO induces targeted degradation of the PML moiety and promotes apoptosis; serial ECG monitoring is mandatory to prevent fatal Torsades de Pointes from QTc prolongation.

modules.name: APML ATRA dosing and favourable risk AML

topics.title: Acute promyelocytic leukaemia ATRA dosing and favourable risk AML with transplant decisions
topics.book: NCCN AML 2024; ELN 2022; WHO 5th Edition

mustKnow.fact: APML carries t(15;17) fusing PML with RARA, freezing maturation and causing DIC, and ATRA forces blast maturation into neutrophils.
Adult ATRA dose in APML is 45 mg per square metre per day orally in two divided doses until complete remission, with arsenic trioxide 0.15 mg per kg per day IV in low and intermediate risk disease.
Children and adolescents under 20 years receive reduced ATRA 25 mg per square metre per day to lower pseudotumour cerebri risk.
AML with t(8;21) RUNX1::RUNX1T1 shows M2 morphology with Auer rods and aberrant CD19 or CD56 yet carries favourable risk with about 90% remission.
A somatic RUNX1 point mutation is adverse risk and must not be confused with the favourable RUNX1::RUNX1T1 fusion.
inv(16) CBFB::MYH11 M4 with abnormal eosinophils is favourable and both core binding factor AMLs benefit from gemtuzumab ozogamicin with HiDAC.
High-burden KIT mutation or persistent MRD in favourable AML pushes the patient to allogeneic transplant in first remission.
Allogeneic transplant in first remission is standard for intermediate and adverse risk AML while favourable risk takes chemotherapy consolidation.

topics.title: Acute lymphoblastic leukaemia
topics.book: DeVita 12e Ch. 70 (Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia)

mustKnow.fact: Acute lymphoblastic leukaemia ALL is immunophenotypically classified into B-cell lineage B-ALL expressing CD19, CD22, CD79a, TdT and T-cell lineage T-ALL expressing cytoplasmic CD3 and CD7.
Philadelphia chromosome-positive Ph+ ALL harbouring t(9;22) BCR-ABL1 requires incorporation of potent BCR-ABL tyrosine kinase inhibitors dasatinib or ponatinib into frontline chemotherapy.
Blinatumomab CD19/CD3 bispecific T-cell engager achieves high minimal residual disease MRD clearance, significantly improving overall survival in relapsed/refractory B-ALL in the TOWER trial.
Inotuzumab ozogamicin is a CD22-directed antibody-drug conjugate with calicheamicin payload, achieving higher complete remission rates than chemotherapy in relapsed B-ALL in the INO-VATE trial.
Tisagenlecleucel autologous anti-CD19 chimeric antigen receptor CAR-T cell therapy induces deep, durable remissions in relapsed/refractory pediatric and young adult B-ALL in the ELIANA trial.
Minimal residual disease MRD assessment by multiparameter flow cytometry or NGS-based immunoglobulin rearrangement is the most powerful independent prognostic predictor in ALL.
CNS prophylaxis comprising intrathecal methotrexate, cytarabine, and hydrocortisone triple intrathecal therapy is mandatory for all ALL patients to prevent leptomeningeal relapse.
L-asparaginase toxicity monitoring requires surveillance for acute pancreatitis, hyperammonemia, hepatic dysfunction, and thrombosis secondary to antithrombin III depletion.

modules.name: Childhood ALL genetics, MRD science and CNS relapse

topics.title: Childhood ALL genetics, MRD science, LP safety, asparaginase biology and CNS relapse
topics.book: NCCN Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia Guidelines 2024; WHO 5th Edition Haematolymphoid Tumours

mustKnow.fact: ETV6::RUNX1 fusion from t(12;21)(p13;q22) is the commonest translocation in childhood B-ALL at about 25%, peaks at age 2 to 9 years, is cryptic on routine karyotype and needs FISH or PCR, and carries a favourable prognosis above 90% event-free survival.
MRD is the strongest independent prognostic factor in ALL with a standard positivity cutoff of 10 to the power minus 4 (0.01%) by flow cytometry or PCR.
NGS (clonoSEQ) with sensitivity to 10 to the power minus 6 is the most sensitive MRD assay in ALL, deeper than flow cytometry and PCR.

Persistent MRD positivity in B-ALL is treated by risk escalation plus blinatumomab, a CD19 by CD3 bispecific T-cell engager, which converts about 4 in 5 MRD-positive patients to negative in the BLAST study.
IMWG MRD negativity in multiple myeloma requires sensitivity of 10 to the power minus 5 or deeper by EuroFlow next-generation flow or NGS on bone marrow.
AML molecular MRD tracks NPM1, RUNX1::RUNX1T1, CBFB::MYH11 and PML::RARA and excludes DTA mutations DNMT3A, TET2 and ASXL1 from clonal haematopoiesis.
Lumbar puncture or intrathecal chemotherapy in leukaemia requires platelets of 50,000 per microlitre or more after transfusion to avoid spinal haematoma and blast seeding of spinal fluid.
L-asparaginase kills ALL blasts, which lack asparagine synthetase, by hydrolysing asparagine to aspartate and ammonia.

Asparaginase glutaminase activity causes acute pancreatitis, which permanently bans rechallenge, and thrombosis from antithrombin, protein C and protein S loss, classically cerebral sinus vein thrombosis.
New headache with cranial nerve palsy in treated ALL means CNS leptomeningeal relapse until proven otherwise and needs urgent spinal fluid cytology with flow cytometry plus marrow biopsy.

topics.title: Chronic myeloid leukaemia
topics.book: DeVita 12e Ch. 71 (Chronic Myeloid Leukemia)

mustKnow.fact: Chronic myeloid leukaemia CML is defined cytogenetically by the Philadelphia chromosome t(9;22)(q34.1;q11.2) creating the constitutively active BCR-ABL1 tyrosine kinase fusion oncogene.
First-generation TKI imatinib 400 mg daily revolutionized CML management, establishing 10-year overall survival exceeding 85% in the landmark IRIS trial.
Second-generation TKIs dasatinib, nilotinib, and bosutinib achieve faster and deeper molecular responses than imatinib, indicated for upfront high-risk disease or imatinib intolerance.
The BCR-ABL1 gatekeeper mutation T315I confers resistance to imatinib, dasatinib, nilotinib, and bosutinib, requiring treatment with third-generation TKI ponatinib.
Asciminib is a first-in-class Specifically Targeting the ABL Myristoyl Pocket STAMP inhibitor, demonstrating superior major molecular response over bosutinib in ASCEMBL and ASC4FIRST.
European LeukemiaNet ELN molecular response milestones define optimal response as BCR-ABL1 transcript 10% or less at 3 months, 1% or less at 6 months, and 0.1% or less MMR at 12 months.
Treatment-free remission TFR is safely feasible in patients maintaining deep molecular response MR4 or MR4.5 for at least 2 years, with successful sustained remission in approximately 50%.
Blast phase CML is defined by 20% or more blasts in marrow/blood or extramedullary blastic involvement, categorized into myeloid 70% and lymphoid 30% blast transformation.

topics.title: Chronic lymphocytic leukaemia
topics.book: DeVita 12e Ch. 72 (Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia and Hairy Cell Leukemia)

mustKnow.fact: Chronic lymphocytic leukaemia CLL is defined by a clonal B-lymphocyte count of 5 x 10^9/L or higher in peripheral blood co-expressing CD5, CD19, CD20, and CD23 with weak surface immunoglobulin.
TP53 aberrations 17p deletion and TP53 mutation and unmutated IGHV status confer aggressive disease course and chemoimmunotherapy resistance.
CLL staging utilizes Rai and Binet systems based on lymphocytosis, lymphadenopathy, organomegaly, anaemia haemoglobin under 10 or 11 g/dL, and thrombocytopenia platelets under 100 x 10^9/L.
Bruton tyrosine kinase BTK inhibitors ibrutinib, acalabrutinib, and zanubrutinib establish superior progression-free survival over chemoimmunotherapy across frontline and relapsed CLL.
Time-limited frontline venetoclax plus obinutuzumab for 12 months demonstrates significant progression-free and overall survival superiority over chlorambucil-obinutuzumab in the CLL14 trial.
Richter transformation describes the rapid clinicopathological transformation of CLL into an aggressive diffuse large B-cell lymphoma in 2% to 10% of patients, carrying poor prognosis.
Autoimmune complications in CLL include autoimmune haemolytic anaemia AIHA with positive direct antiglobulin test and immune thrombocytopenic purpura ITP, managed with corticosteroids.
Hairy cell leukaemia is an indolent B-cell neoplasm marked by pancytopenia, splenomegaly, dry bone marrow tap, and ubiquitous BRAF V600E mutations, exquisitely sensitive to cladribine.

modules.name: Chronic leukemias across CLL and CML

topics.title: Chronic leukemias: CLL watchful waiting and del17p therapy, CML transcripts and blast phase
topics.book: iwCLL Guidelines; NCCN CLL 2024; NCCN CML 2024; WHO 5th Edition

mustKnow.fact: Asymptomatic early-stage CLL is managed with watchful waiting until iwCLL active disease criteria develop, even with high-risk genetics like del(17p).

iwCLL treatment triggers are haemoglobin under 10, platelets under 100,000, spleen 6 cm or more, nodes 10 cm or more, lymphocyte doubling under 6 months, B symptoms, and steroid-refractory autoimmune cytopenias.
Isolated hypogammaglobulinemia never starts CLL therapy and recurrent infections with it are treated with IVIG replacement.
Falling counts in CLL need a Coombs test plus marrow examination to separate autoimmune destruction treated with steroids from Rai stage 3 or 4 infiltration treated with CLL therapy.
CLL with del(17p) or TP53 mutation forbids FCR and bendamustine rituximab and uses zanubrutinib, acalabrutinib, or venetoclax with obinutuzumab first line.
Ibrutinib is not preferred first line in CLL because of higher atrial fibrillation, hypertension and bleeding than second-generation BTK blockers.
BCR::ABL1 e13a2 and e14a2 transcripts make p210 protein in classic CML, e1a2 makes p190 in Philadelphia-positive ALL, and e19a2 makes p230 in neutrophilic CML.
CML with 20 percent or more blasts in blood or marrow or extramedullary myeloid sarcoma is blast phase, and WHO 5th edition abolished accelerated phase.

topics.title: Myeloproliferative neoplasms and myelodysplastic syndromes
topics.book: DeVita 12e Ch. 73 (Myelodysplastic Syndromes and Myeloproliferative Neoplasms)

mustKnow.fact: Classical BCR-ABL1-negative myeloproliferative neoplasms polycythaemia vera PV, essential thrombocythaemia ET, and primary myelofibrosis PMF are driven by somatic mutations in JAK2, CALR, or MPL.
JAK2 V617F point mutation in exon 14 is present in over 95% of polycythaemia vera patients and approximately 50% to 60% of patients with essential thrombocythaemia and primary myelofibrosis.
Polycythaemia vera diagnostic criteria mandate haemoglobin over 16.5 g/dL in men or 16.0 g/dL in women, bone marrow panmyelosis, and presence of JAK2 mutation.

Therapeutic phlebotomy maintaining hematocrit strictly below 45% combined with low-dose aspirin significantly reduces cardiovascular death and major thrombotic events in polycythaemia vera in CYTO-PV.

Ruxolitinib oral JAK1/JAK2 inhibitor significantly reduces splenomegaly, alleviates constitutional symptoms, and improves survival in intermediate- and high-risk myelofibrosis in COMFORT-I and COMFORT-II.
Myelodysplastic syndromes MDS are characterized by peripheral cytopenias, dysplastic bone marrow morphology, and risk of transformation into acute myeloid leukaemia.
The Molecular International Prognostic Scoring System IPSS-M integrates multi-gene somatic mutations with cytogenetics and blast count, refining risk stratification in MDS.
Lenalidomide induces high rates of transfusion independence and cytogenetic remissions in lower-risk MDS with isolated del(5q) chromosomal abnormality.

topics.title: Hodgkin lymphoma
topics.book: DeVita 12e Ch. 66 (Hodgkin Lymphoma)

mustKnow.fact: Classical Hodgkin lymphoma cHL is pathologically characterized by multinucleated Reed-Sternberg cells expressing CD15 and CD30 while typically lacking CD20 and CD45 leukocyte common antigen.
First-line chemotherapy for classical Hodgkin lymphoma standardly comprises ABVD doxorubicin, bleomycin, vinblastine, and dacarbazine or escalated BEACOPP in high-risk advanced disease.
Interim PET-CT adapted therapy following 2 cycles of ABVD in the RATHL trial allows safe omission of bleomycin in PET-negative patients Deauville 1 to 3, eliminating bleomycin lung toxicity.
Brentuximab vedotin anti-CD30 antibody-drug conjugate combined with AVD significantly improves overall survival over ABVD in advanced stage III or IV Hodgkin lymphoma in ECHELON-1.
Nivolumab plus AVD significantly improved progression-free survival and reduced toxicities compared to brentuximab vedotin plus AVD in advanced stage classical Hodgkin lymphoma in SWOG S1826.
Nodular lymphocyte predominant Hodgkin lymphoma NLPHL features neoplastic popcorn lymphocytic and histiocytic LP cells expressing CD20 and B-cell transcription factors, managed differently from cHL.

Involved-site radiotherapy ISRT delivers reduced radiation fields constrained strictly to initially involved lymph node volumes, markedly minimizing late cardiovascular and secondary malignancy risks.
Late survivorship complications after Hodgkin lymphoma treatment include accelerated coronary artery disease, premature heart failure, and secondary breast or thyroid carcinomas.

modules.name: Hodgkin lymphoma survivorship, salvage and fertility

topics.title: Hodgkin lymphoma survivorship, second cancers, ABVD toxicity, relapse salvage and fertility
topics.book: NCCN Hodgkin Lymphoma Guidelines 2024; NCCN Survivorship Guidelines

mustKnow.fact: Second primary malignancy is the number one cause of late mortality in cured Hodgkin lymphoma survivors, followed by cardiovascular disease in second place.
Therapy-related AML and MDS from alkylating chemotherapy, often with chromosome 5 or 7 deletions, peak 5 to 10 years after Hodgkin treatment.
Radiation-induced solid tumours, led by breast cancer in women irradiated to the chest before age 30, peak 15 to 20 years after treatment and rise for decades.
Female chest-irradiated survivors need yearly breast MRI plus yearly mammography starting 8 years after radiation or at age 25, whichever comes later.
Doxorubicin cardiotoxicity in ABVD is screened with baseline echocardiography.
Bleomycin pulmonary fibrosis in ABVD is screened with baseline lung function testing including DLCO.
Vinblastine in ABVD causes peripheral and autonomic neuropathy with constipation and ileus, while dacarbazine causes severe emesis and myelosuppression with rare secondary leukaemia.
Relapsed or refractory classical Hodgkin lymphoma is treated with salvage chemo-immunotherapy such as ICE, DHAP or GVD with brentuximab vedotin or PD-1 blockade to a PET-negative response.
Salvage response in Hodgkin lymphoma is consolidated with high-dose BEAM chemotherapy followed by autologous stem cell transplant.
ABVD carries under 5% lasting infertility with no added birth defect or miscarriage risk, but sperm banking precedes cycle one because escalation to BEACOPP causes azoospermia in over 80%.

topics.title: Aggressive B cell lymphomas
topics.book: DeVita 12e Ch. 67 (Aggressive B-Cell Non-Hodgkin Lymphomas)

mustKnow.fact: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma DLBCL is the most common non-Hodgkin lymphoma, divided by cell of origin into germinal centre B-cell-like GCB and activated B-cell-like ABC phenotypes.
Frontline R-CHOP rituximab, cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, vincristine, prednisone cures approximately 60% of patients with advanced diffuse large B-cell lymphoma.
Polatuzumab vedotin anti-CD79b antibody-drug conjugate substituted for vincristine in Pola-R-CHP significantly improves progression-free survival over R-CHOP in previously untreated DLBCL in POLARIX.
High-grade B-cell lymphoma with MYC and BCL2 and/or BCL6 rearrangements double-hit or triple-hit lymphoma exhibits an aggressive clinical course resistant to standard R-CHOP.
The International Prognostic Index IPI incorporates age over 60, stage III/IV, elevated LDH, ECOG performance status 2 or higher, and more than 1 extranodal site.
Burkitt lymphoma is a high-grade B-cell malignancy with near 100% Ki-67 proliferation and hallmark MYC translocations t(8;14), exhibiting a characteristic starry-sky histological pattern.

Autologous CAR-T cell therapy axicabtagene ciloleucel in ZUMA-7 and lisocabtagene maraleucel in TRANSFORM established significant event-free and overall survival superiority over salvage autologous transplant in early-relapsed DLBCL.
Mantle cell lymphoma MCL is defined by t(11;14)(q13;q32) producing cyclin D1 CCND1 nuclear overexpression, displaying high sensitivity to covalent BTK inhibitors ibrutinib and zanubrutinib.

topics.title: Indolent B cell lymphomas
topics.book: DeVita 12e Ch. 67 (Indolent B-Cell Lymphomas and Waldenström Macroglobulinemia)

mustKnow.fact: Follicular lymphoma FL is the most common indolent non-Hodgkin lymphoma, defined by the hallmark t(14;18)(q32;q21) translocation placing BCL2 under immunoglobulin heavy chain enhancer control.
The Follicular Lymphoma International Prognostic Index FLIPI stratifies risk based on age over 60, stage III/IV, anaemia under 12 g/dL, more than 4 nodal areas, and elevated serum LDH.
Asymptomatic, low tumour burden follicular lymphoma is safely managed with watch-and-wait surveillance without compromising overall survival.
Symptomatic advanced follicular lymphoma is standardly treated with bendamustine plus rituximab BR or R-CHOP, with BR demonstrating superior progression-free survival in the StiL trial.

Gastric mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue MALT lymphoma is strongly driven by chronic Helicobacter pylori infection; eradication therapy with antibiotics induces complete lymphoma remission in over 75% of early cases.
Waldenstrom macroglobulinemia is a lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma producing monoclonal IgM paraprotein, carrying the signature somatic activating MYD88 L265P mutation in over 90% of cases.

Histological transformation of indolent follicular lymphoma into aggressive diffuse large B-cell lymphoma occurs at approximately 2% to 3% per year, heralded by rapid nodal growth, fever, and soaring LDH.
Mosunetuzumab is a CD20/CD3 bispecific T-cell engaging antibody inducing high, durable complete response rates in relapsed or refractory follicular lymphoma after two or more prior lines.

modules.name: T cell and NK cell lymphomas

topics.title: T cell and NK cell lymphomas
topics.book: DeVita 12e Ch. 68 (T-Cell and Natural Killer Cell Neoplasms)

mustKnow.fact: Peripheral T-cell lymphomas PTCL are an aggressive, heterogeneous group of mature post-thymic lymphoid malignancies expressing CD2, CD3, CD5, and CD7 with T-cell receptor gene rearrangements.
Anaplastic large cell lymphoma ALCL is divided into ALK-positive driven by t(2;5)(p23;q35) NPM1-ALK with favourable prognosis and ALK-negative exhibiting inferior survival outcomes.
Brentuximab vedotin added to CHP cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, prednisone established significant progression-free and overall survival superiority over CHOP in CD30-positive PTCL in ECHELON-2.

Angioimmunoblastic T-cell lymphoma AITL originates from follicular helper T cells, characterized by generalized lymphadenopathy, autoimmune hemolytic anemia, polyclonal hypergammaglobulinemia, and RHOA or TET2 mutations.

Extranodal NK/T-cell lymphoma nasal type is an aggressive, destructive midline midfacial malignancy universally driven by Epstein-Barr virus EBV infection, requiring non-cross-resistant L-asparaginase regimens.

Mycosis fungoides is the most common cutaneous T-cell lymphoma CTCL, presenting with progressive indolent cutaneous patches, plaques, and tumours containing atypical cerebriform Pautrier microabscesses.
Sezary syndrome is the leukemic variant of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma defined by generalized pruritic erythroderma, lymphadenopathy, and circulating clonally identical cerebriform Sezary cells.
Adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma ATLL is caused by human T-cell lymphotropic virus type 1 HTLV-1, presenting with aggressive lymphocytosis, lytic bone lesions, and refractory hypercalcaemia.

modules.name: Multiple myeloma and plasma cell disorders

topics.title: Multiple myeloma and plasma cell disorders
topics.book: DeVita 12e Ch. 74 (Plasma Cell Neoplasms and Amyloidosis)

mustKnow.fact: Multiple myeloma diagnosis requires clonal bone marrow plasma cells of 10% or more or biopsy-proven plasmacytoma plus at least one CRAB or SLiM myeloma-defining event.
SLiM criteria comprise Sixty percent or greater clonal marrow plasma cells, involved-to-uninvolved serum Free Light Chain ratio 100 or higher, and more than 1 focal MRI bone lesion.
The Revised International Staging System R-ISS incorporates serum beta-2 microglobulin, albumin, LDH, and high-risk cytogenetics del(17p), t(4;14), and t(14;16) into stages I to III.

Frontline quadruplet therapy combining anti-CD38 monoclonal antibody daratumumab or isatuximab with bortezomib, lenalidomide, and dexamethasone DVRd significantly deepens MRD-negative remissions in GRIFFIN and PERSEUS.
High-dose melphalan 200 mg/m2 conditioning followed by autologous stem cell transplantation ASCT remains the standard consolidative therapy for transplant-eligible multiple myeloma in DETERMINATION.
Teclistamab is a BCMAxCD3 bispecific T-cell engager antibody approved for relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma, inducing deep and durable overall response rates exceeding 60% in MajesTEC-1.

Ciltacabtagene autoleucel cilta-cel anti-BCMA CAR-T cell therapy demonstrated significant overall survival superiority over standard-of-care pomalidomide regimens in early relapsed myeloma in CARTITUDE-4.
Monoclonal gammopathy of undetermined significance MGUS is defined by serum M-protein under 3 g/dL, clonal bone marrow plasma cells under 10%, and complete absence of end-organ damage.

modules.name: Myeloma cytogenetic risk, renal failure and IMiDs

topics.title: Myeloma cytogenetic risk, renal failure induction and IMiD potency with safety
topics.book: IMWG Criteria; NCCN Multiple Myeloma 2024

mustKnow.fact: Standard-risk myeloma cytogenetics are hyperdiploidy or trisomies, t(11;14) and t(6;14).
High-risk myeloma cytogenetics are t(4;14), t(14;16), t(14;20), del(17p) and gain of 1q21.
t(11;14) drives cyclin D1 and BCL2 addiction and predicts venetoclax sensitivity in myeloma.

Myeloma with acute renal failure from cast nephropathy plus hypercalcaemia is induced urgently with bortezomib, cyclophosphamide and dexamethasone (VCD / CyBorD) with or without daratumumab plus saline hydration.
Bortezomib and cyclophosphamide clear hepatically and need no renal dose cut, while full-dose lenalidomide is renally cleared and avoided in acute renal failure.
Pomalidomide is the most potent IMiD at about 10 times lenalidomide, overcomes lenalidomide resistance, and is hepatically metabolised so it stays full dose in renal impairment.
All IMiDs need VTE thromboprophylaxis, pomalidomide and lenalidomide cause neutropenia, and thalidomide causes neuropathy.
Pomalidomide is dosed 4 mg on days 1 to 21 of each 28-day cycle.

topics.title: Haematopoietic stem cell transplantation
topics.book: DeVita 12e Ch. 21 (Stem Cell Transplantation and Cellular Therapy)

mustKnow.fact: Autologous haematopoietic stem cell transplantation ASCT delivers supralethal myeloablative chemotherapy followed by infusion of the patient's own cryopreserved stem cells to restore haematopoiesis.
Allogeneic haematopoietic cell transplantation allo-HCT relies on the donor immune system to exert a powerful, curative graft-versus-leukaemia GVL or graft-versus-malignancy immunologic effect.
Human leukocyte antigen HLA matching at 8 of 8 or 10 of 10 high-resolution loci HLA-A, B, C, DRB1, and DQB1 minimizes graft failure and graft-versus-host disease GVHD risk.

Haploidentical stem cell transplantation utilizing post-transplant cyclophosphamide PTCy on days +3 and +4 selectively eliminates alloreactive T-lymphocytes while preserving regulatory and stem cell compartments.
Acute graft-versus-host disease aGVHD manifests within the first 100 days involving the skin maculopapular rash, liver cholestatic hyperbilirubinemia, and gastrointestinal tract secretory diarrhoea.
mustKnow.source: Mount Sinai Acute GVHD International Consortium (MAGIC)

mustKnow.fact: Ruxolitinib JAK1/JAK2 inhibitor significantly improves overall response rates and survival in acute and chronic steroid-refractory GVHD in the REACH2 and REACH3 trials.
Sinusoidal obstruction syndrome SOS / veno-occlusive disease VOD is characterised by painful hepatomegaly, jaundice, and fluid retention, successfully treated with defibrotide.
Cytomegalovirus CMV reactivation following allogeneic transplantation is monitored with serial quantitative PCR and treated with preemptive ganciclovir, or prevented with letermovir prophylaxis.

modules.name: NHL subtyping and staging, HLH, chronic GVHD and polycythaemia

topics.title: NHL subtyping and staging, HLH, chronic GVHD and polycythaemia diagnosis
topics.book: DeVita 12e Ch. 103 (Non-Hodgkin Lymphomas); Ch. 104 (Hodgkin Lymphoma); Ch. 22 (Myeloproliferative Neoplasms)

mustKnow.fact: The Hans algorithm orders CD10 then BCL6 then MUM1, and CD10 positivity defines germinal centre GCB type diffuse large B cell lymphoma.
CD10 negative with BCL6 negative, or CD10 negative with BCL6 positive and MUM1 positive, defines non-GCB or activated B cell ABC type.
Activated B cell ABC type fares worse with R-CHOP and gains most from polatuzumab based Pola-R-CHP tested in POLARIX.
Gastric MALT lymphoma starts with H pylori eradication, giving complete remission in 75 to 80 percent of stage one and two cases.
The t(11;18) swap creating BIRC3 with MALT1 predicts antibiotic failure, moving care to involved site radiotherapy or rituximab, and radical gastrectomy is obsolete.
Lugano treats the spleen as a lymphatic organ, so nodes on both sides of the diaphragm plus spleen plus B symptoms is stage IIIBS and never stage four.
Lugano abolished the X suffix for bulky disease and keeps A and B suffixes only for Hodgkin lymphoma.
HLH needs at least five of eight HLH-2004 criteria including high triglycerides at least 265 mg/dL or low fibrinogen 1.5 g/L or below, ferritin at least 500 ng/mL and soluble CD25 at least 2400 U/mL.
Chronic graft versus host disease runs through thymic damage, regulatory T cell deficiency and aberrant B cell autoantibody production driving transforming growth factor beta fibrosis.
Total body irradiation belongs to acute lymphoblastic leukaemia conditioning for sanctuary sites, not to myeloid conditioning.
True polycythaemia shows raised red cell mass with normal or expanded plasma volume, normal oxygen saturation, suppressed erythropoietin EPO and usually JAK2 V617F mutation in over 95 percent.

topics.title: Paediatric solid tumours
topics.book: DeVita 12e Ch. 59 (Principles of Pediatric Solid Tumors)

mustKnow.fact: Neuroblastoma is the most common extracranial solid tumour of infancy, originating from neural crest sympathoadrenal progenitor cells in the adrenal medulla or sympathetic chain.
MYCN proto-oncogene amplification greater than 4-fold is the most powerful molecular marker of high-risk neuroblastoma, predicting rapid disease progression and chemotherapy resistance.
Dinutuximab anti-GD2 chimeric monoclonal antibody combined with GM-CSF and interleukin-2 significantly improves event-free and overall survival in high-risk neuroblastoma in ANBL0032.
Wilms tumour nephroblastoma is the most common paediatric renal malignancy, strongly associated with WT1 mutations on chromosome 11p13 in WAGR and Denys-Drash syndromes.
Retinoblastoma arises from biallelic inactivation of the RB1 tumour suppressor gene on chromosome 13q14, presenting classically as leukocoria cat's eye reflex and strabismus.

Hepatoblastoma is the most common liver malignancy in infants and young children, associated with Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome and familial adenomatous polyposis, presenting with markedly elevated serum AFP.
Rhabdomyosarcoma is the most common soft tissue sarcoma of childhood, divided histologically into favourable embryonal RMS with 11p15 loss and high-risk alveolar RMS with FOXO1 translocations.

Medulloblastoma standard management combines maximal safe surgical resection, craniospinal irradiation, and multi-agent platinum-alkylator chemotherapy, with cure rates exceeding 70% in standard-risk disease.

modules.name: Geriatric oncology, AYA and cancer in pregnancy

topics.title: Geriatric oncology, AYA and cancer in pregnancy
topics.book: DeVita 12e Ch. 65 (Adolescent, Young Adult and Geriatric Oncology)

mustKnow.fact: Comprehensive Geriatric Assessment CGA evaluates functional status, comorbidities, cognition, nutritional state, polypharmacy, and social support, identifying vulnerabilities missed by ECOG performance status.
The G8 screening questionnaire is a validated 8-item tool where scores of 14 or less indicate impaired functional reserve warranting in-depth comprehensive geriatric evaluation.
The Cancer and Aging Research Group CARG toxicity score predicts severe grade 3 to 5 chemotherapy-related toxicities in older adults based on clinical and laboratory parameters.
Adolescent and young adult AYA oncology addresses distinct biological entities, clinical trial underrepresentation, and unique survivorship, fertility, and psychosocial needs.
Fertility preservation counseling is mandatory prior to initiating gonadotoxic chemotherapy, offering sperm cryopreservation for postpubertal males and oocyte or embryo cryopreservation for females.

GnRH agonists goserelin or leuprolide administered during adjuvant chemotherapy significantly reduce premature ovarian insufficiency and improve subsequent pregnancy rates in young breast cancer patients.

Chemotherapy in pregnancy can be safely administered starting in the second trimester after organogenesis is complete, whereas methotrexate and radiotherapy are strictly contraindicated during pregnancy.
mustKnow.source: ESMO Guidelines on Cancer in Pregnancy

mustKnow.fact: Physiological pharmacokinetic changes in pregnancy including expanded plasma volume and enhanced renal clearance alter chemotherapy distribution and clearance, but standard dosing based on actual body weight is recommended.

topics.title: Survivorship and late effects
topics.book: DeVita 12e Ch. 104 (Cancer Survivorship and Late Treatment Complications)

mustKnow.fact: Second malignant neoplasms SMN represent a major cause of late non-relapse mortality among long-term cancer survivors, driven by prior radiation therapy and alkylating chemotherapy.
Therapy-related acute myeloid leukaemia t-AML following topoisomerase II inhibitors etoposide typically manifests after a short latency of 1 to 3 years with balanced 11q23 MLL rearrangements.

Female childhood cancer survivors treated with chest irradiation before age 30 carry an elevated breast cancer risk comparable to BRCA mutation carriers, requiring annual screening MRI starting at age 25.
Chemotherapy-related cognitive impairment CRCI chemo brain causes subtle deficits in executive functioning, memory, and processing speed, responsive to cognitive rehabilitation.
Radiation-induced fibrosis RIF causes progressive subcutaneous induration, microvascular damage, and organ dysfunction, partially ameliorated by combination pentoxifylline and vitamin E.
Exercise oncology interventions consisting of structured aerobic and resistance training significantly reduce cancer-related fatigue and improve cardiovascular fitness and quality of life.

Financial toxicity in cancer care encompasses objective out-of-pocket costs and subjective financial distress, which independently correlate with treatment non-adherence and inferior overall survival.
Individualized cancer survivorship care plans summarizing previous treatments, potential late sequelae, and detailed surveillance schedules ensure seamless transition to primary care.

topics.title: Anthracycline cardiotoxicity: thresholds, pathology, mechanism and prevention
topics.book: DeVita 12e Ch. 94 (Cardiovascular Toxicities of Cancer Treatment)

mustKnow.fact: Maximum lifetime cumulative doses are epirubicin 900 mg/m2, daunorubicin 550 to 600, doxorubicin 450 to 550, idarubicin 150 and mitoxantrone 140.
Epirubicin allows the highest total through glucuronidation with less intramyocardial free radical generation.
Adria cells show cytoplasmic vacuolar degeneration on light microscopy and myofibrillar loss with Z band disruption on electron microscopy, graded by the Billingham scale.
Classic anthracycline cardiomyopathy is cumulative and dose dependent and most commonly declares itself within 1 year after completing therapy.
Doxorubicin heart failure rates run about 3 to 5 percent at 400 mg/m2, 4 to 7 percent at 500 to 550 and above 36 percent at 600 or more.
Antitumour action runs through DNA intercalation and topoisomerase II alpha blockade while cardiac injury runs through the beta isoform.
Cardiac injury flows from iron catalysed reactive oxygen species plus cardiomyocyte topoisomerase II beta poisoning, and dexrazoxane prevents both arms.
TOP2A sits beside ERBB2 HER2 on chromosome 17q12 to 21 and is co amplified in 35 to 40 percent of HER2 positive breast cancers.
Proven cardioprotection means dexrazoxane once doxorubicin exceeds 300 mg/m2 at a 10 to 1 dose ratio, liposomal doxorubicin or continuous infusion over 6 to 96 hours lowering peaks.
Ivabradine does not prevent cardiomyopathy and is the classic EXCEPT answer among protectors.
ESC defines cancer therapy related cardiac dysfunction as a left ventricular ejection fraction drop above 10 points to below 50 percent or a relative global longitudinal strain fall above 15 percent.

topics.title: Cardio-oncology
topics.book: DeVita 12e Ch. 94 (Cardiovascular Toxicities of Cancer Treatment)

mustKnow.fact: Anthracycline-induced cardiotoxicity type I is cumulative, dose-dependent, and associated with permanent myocardial ultrastructural damage and myocyte loss.
Dexrazoxane is an intracellular iron-chelating agent that prevents free radical generation, approved as a cardioprotective agent for cumulative doxorubicin doses exceeding 300 mg/m2.
Trastuzumab cardiotoxicity type II is not dose-dependent, characteristically non-structural and reversible upon drug interruption and initiation of ACE inhibitors and beta-blockers.

Echocardiographic global longitudinal strain GLS detects early subclinical myocardial dysfunction; a relative reduction greater than 15% from baseline predicts subsequent left ventricular ejection fraction decline.

Immune checkpoint inhibitor-associated myocarditis is a fulminant, life-threatening complication with mortality approaching 50%, requiring immediate high-dose intravenous methylprednisolone 1,000 mg daily.
Fluoropyrimidines 5-FU and capecitabine can trigger coronary vasospasm and myocardial ischemia, managed by immediate drug cessation, nitrates, and calcium channel blockers.
VEGF inhibitors bevacizumab, sunitinib, and axitinib frequently induce systemic arterial hypertension in up to 80% of patients through endothelial nitric oxide reduction and capillary rarefaction.
Baseline and serial QTc interval monitoring is mandatory for patients receiving targeted tyrosine kinase inhibitors like ribociclib, sunitinib, or vandetanib, intervening when QTc exceeds 500 ms.

topics.title: Myelosuppression and febrile neutropenia
topics.book: DeVita 12e Ch. 90 (Neutropenia, Thrombocytopenia and Colony-Stimulating Factors)

mustKnow.fact: Febrile neutropenia is defined as an absolute neutrophil count ANC under 500 cells/microL or expected to fall below 500 within 48 hours, with a single oral temperature of 38.3 C or 38.0 C over 1 hour.
The Multinational Association for Supportive Care in Cancer MASCC index identifies low-risk febrile neutropenia eligible for outpatient oral antibiotic therapy with a score of 21 or higher.
The Clinical Index of Stable Febrile Neutropenia CISNE score specifically stratifies solid tumour patients presenting with febrile neutropenia to identify candidates for outpatient care.
High-risk febrile neutropenia mandates immediate inpatient empirical monotherapy with an antipseudomonal beta-lactam such as piperacillin-tazobactam, cefepime, or meropenem within 1 hour.
Primary prophylaxis with granulocyte colony-stimulating factors G-CSF filgrastim or pegfilgrastim is recommended when the anticipated regimen risk of febrile neutropenia is 20% or higher.
Posaconazole primary antifungal prophylaxis is standard for high-risk neutropenic patients undergoing remission induction for AML or MDS to prevent invasive aspergillosis.
Erythropoiesis-stimulating agents ESAs are indicated only for palliative chemotherapy-induced anaemia with haemoglobin under 10 g/dL, avoiding use when cure is the anticipated outcome.
Platelet transfusions are indicated prophylactically at a threshold of 10 x 10^9/L or lower in stable hypoproliferative thrombocytopenia, and at 20 x 10^9/L in the presence of fever or bleeding.

topics.title: Chemotherapy induced nausea and vomiting
topics.book: DeVita 12e Ch. 91 (Chemotherapy-Induced Nausea and Vomiting)

mustKnow.fact: Chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting CINV is categorized chronologically into acute occurring within 24 hours, delayed occurring from 24 to 120 hours, and anticipatory emesis.
Highly emetogenic chemotherapy HEC such as cisplatin or AC combinations triggers vomiting in over 90% of patients without antiemetic prophylaxis.
The standard frontline 4-drug antiemetic regimen for highly emetogenic chemotherapy combines an NK1 receptor antagonist, a 5-HT3 receptor antagonist, dexamethasone, and olanzapine.
Neurokinin-1 NK1 receptor antagonists aprepitant, fosaprepitant, and rolapitant block substance P binding in the area postrema, specifically preventing delayed emesis.
Palonosetron is a second-generation 5-HT3 receptor antagonist featuring an extended half-life of 40 hours and allosteric receptor binding, outperforming older 5-HT3 antagonists in delayed emesis.
Olanzapine 5 to 10 mg daily significantly reduces acute and delayed nausea and vomiting when added to standard triplets for highly emetogenic chemotherapy in the NEJM trial by Navari et al.
Anticipatory nausea is a conditioned response conditioned by previous poorly controlled emetic episodes, best prevented by optimal upfront emetic control and treated with oral lorazepam.
Cannabinoids and metoclopramide are reserved as second-line breakthrough antiemetics for refractory nausea and vomiting not controlled by primary antiemetic regimens.

topics.title: Organ-specific toxicities of cytotoxics
topics.book: DeVita 12e Ch. 92 & 95 (Organ-Specific Toxicities of Cytotoxic Agents)

mustKnow.fact: Anthracycline cardiotoxicity is mediated by topoisomerase II-beta binding and free radical generation, causing irreversible myocyte death and dilated cardiomyopathy.
Bleomycin pulmonary toxicity manifests as subacute pneumonitis progressing to irreversible pulmonary fibrosis, accelerated by high concentrations of supplemental inspired oxygen.
Cisplatin nephrotoxicity causes acute tubular necrosis and magnesium wasting; vigorous intravenous pre- and post-hydration with isotonic saline significantly mitigates nephrotoxic risk.
Ifosfamide neurotoxicity manifests as somnolence, confusion, cerebellar ataxia, and hallucination caused by chloroacetaldehyde metabolites, treated with intravenous methylene blue.
Glucarpidase carboxypeptidase G2 rapidly cleaves circulating methotrexate into inactive DAMPA during toxic methotrexate concentrations in the setting of acute kidney injury.
Oxaliplatin-induced acute neurotoxicity presents as cold-triggered dysaesthesia, perioral numbness, and pharyngolaryngeal dysaesthesia, distinct from chronic cumulative sensory axonopathy.
Irinotecan-induced delayed secretory diarrhoea is mediated by active SN-38 mucosal damage, managed with high-dose loperamide 4 mg initially then 2 mg every 2 hours.
5-Fluorouracil cardiotoxicity manifests as angina, coronary vasospasm, acute coronary syndromes, and cardiogenic shock, requiring immediate infusion cessation and calcium channel blockers.

topics.title: Immune related adverse events
topics.book: DeVita 12e Ch. 18 (Immune-Related Adverse Events of Checkpoint Inhibitors)

mustKnow.fact: Immune-related adverse events irAEs arise from autoimmune breakdown of self-tolerance following CTLA-4, PD-1, or PD-L1 blockade, potentially affecting any organ system.
Checkpoint inhibitor colitis presents with profuse watery diarrhoea and mucosal ulceration; grade 2 or higher colitis requires systemic corticosteroids with prednisone 1 to 2 mg/kg daily.
Steroid-refractory immune colitis failing systemic corticosteroids within 48 to 72 hours requires prompt escalation to anti-TNF antibody infliximab or gut-selective integrin inhibitor vedolizumab.
Immune checkpoint inhibitor pneumonitis manifests as dyspnoea, dry cough, and ground-glass opacities, requiring immediate drug interruption, high-dose steroids, and infectious bronchoscopy workup.

Endocrine irAEs including hypophysitis and thyroiditis are typically irreversible, requiring long-term hormone replacement with levothyroxine or physiological hydrocortisone without discontinuing immunotherapy.
Checkpoint inhibitor-associated hepatitis presents with asymptomatic AST/ALT elevations; steroid-refractory immune hepatitis is treated with oral mycophenolate mofetil rather than infliximab.
Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events CTCAE grades irAE severity from grade 1 mild asymptomatic to grade 4 life-threatening and grade 5 death.

Immune checkpoint inhibitor rechallenge is generally safe for resolved low-grade toxicities but is permanently contraindicated following severe grade 4 irAEs, especially myocarditis and Stevens-Johnson syndrome.

modules.name: Toxicities of targeted agents and ADCs

topics.title: Toxicities of targeted agents and ADCs
topics.book: DeVita 12e Ch. 14 (Toxicities and Monitoring of Targeted Therapies)

mustKnow.fact: EGFR inhibitors cause acneiform papulopustular skin eruptions on sebum-rich areas in up to 90% of patients, treated prophylactically with oral doxycycline or minocycline.
Paronychia and pyogenic granuloma-like periungual lesions represent chronic disabling cutaneous complications of EGFR inhibitors, requiring topical potent steroids and antimicrobial soaks.
Hand-foot skin reaction HFSR associated with multikinase VEGFR inhibitors sorafenib and regorafenib manifests as hyperkeratotic painful tender blisters over mechanical friction pressure points.

Trastuzumab deruxtecan T-DXd carries a major boxed warning for drug-induced interstitial lung disease ILD and pneumonitis, requiring proactive baseline CT, prompt interruption, and corticosteroid management.
mustKnow.source: DESTINY-Breast Guidelines / Powell et al. (ESMO Open)

mustKnow.fact: Alpelisib PI3K-alpha inhibitor frequently causes severe grade 3 to 4 hyperglycemia in over 30% of patients, requiring baseline HbA1c screening and prophylactic metformin.
CDK4/6 inhibitors induce uncomplicated, rapidly reversible bone marrow neutropenia without the true apoptotic marrow depletion typical of traditional cytotoxic chemotherapy.
Lorlatinib ALK inhibitor causes unique central nervous system neurocognitive, mood, and speech adverse effects along with severe hypertriglyceridemia and hypercholesterolemia in over 80%.
Antibody-drug conjugates carrying monomethyl auristatin E MMAE or deruxtecan payloads require vigilance for signature toxicities including peripheral neuropathy, ocular keratitis, and alopecia.

topics.title: Infusion reactions, hypersensitivity and extravasation
topics.book: DeVita 12e Ch. 6 (Hypersensitivity Reactions and Extravasation Management)

mustKnow.fact: Taxane paclitaxel hypersensitivity reactions are acute Type I IgE-independent anaphylactoid reactions driven by vehicle solvent Cremophor EL, prevented by dexamethasone, H1, and H2 antihistamines.
Platinum carboplatin and oxaliplatin hypersensitivity reactions are true Type I IgE-mediated allergies typically emerging after 6 or more treatment cycles, treatable via standardized desensitization.
Cytotoxic extravasation injuries are classified as vesicants causing progressive severe tissue necrosis, irritants causing localized inflammatory discomfort, and non-vesicant harmless infiltrations.
Anthracycline doxorubicin extravasation mandates immediate cold pack application and intravenous administration of the antidote dexrazoxane over 3 consecutive days.
Vinca alkaloid vincristine and vinblastine extravasation requires dry warm compress application to promote vasodilation and local subcutaneous injection of hyaluronidase.
Mechlorethamine nitrogen mustard extravasation is treated with local subcutaneous sodium thiosulfate injections to chemically inactivate remaining reactive alkylating groups.
Totally implantable venous access ports TIVAP reduce peripheral extravasation risks but require strict aseptic technique, regular heparin flushing, and needle verification prior to infusion.
Monoclonal antibody infusion-related reactions rituximab and daratumumab are mediated by systemic cytokine release, treated with temporary infusion interruption, diphenhydramine, and paracetamol.

topics.title: Mucositis, dermatological and gonadal toxicity
topics.book: DeVita 12e Ch. 93 (Oral and Mucocutaneous Toxicities in Oncology)

mustKnow.fact: Oral mucositis is initiated by reactive oxygen species ROS and NF-kappaB activation damaging submucosal vascularity and overlying epithelium following cytotoxic chemotherapy or head/neck irradiation.

Palifermin recombinant human keratinocyte growth factor KGF reduces the incidence, duration, and severity of severe oral mucositis in autologous stem cell transplantation for hematologic malignancies.
Oral cryotherapy holding ice chips in the mouth during bolus 5-fluorouracil or high-dose melphalan induces local vasoconstriction, significantly reducing oral mucositis.
Scalp cooling hypothermia devices induce vasoconstriction of scalp microvessels, reducing follicular cytotoxic drug uptake and preventing chemotherapy-induced alopecia.

Capecitabine and continuous-infusion 5-FU hand-foot syndrome palmar-plantar erythrodysesthesia presents with progressive painful erythema, swelling, and desquamation, responsive to topical urea creams and dose reduction.
Chemotherapy-induced premature ovarian insufficiency POI is age- and dose-dependent, highest with alkylating agents cyclophosphamide, causing amenorrhoea and early menopause.
Alkylating agents cause permanent testicular germinal epithelial atrophy and azoospermia with preservation of Leydig cell testosterone production.
Taxane-induced nail changes include subungual haemorrhage, onycholysis, Beau lines, and painful subungual abscesses, partially prevented by frozen glove application during infusions.

topics.title: Oncologic emergencies
topics.book: DeVita 12e Ch. 79-82 (Oncologic Emergencies: TLS, Hypercalcemia and Cord Compression)

mustKnow.fact: Tumour lysis syndrome TLS Cairo-Bishop laboratory definition requires two or more metabolic derangements within 3 to 7 days: hyperuricaemia, hyperkalaemia, hyperphosphataemia, and secondary hypocalcaemia.
Rasburicase recombinant urate oxidase rapidly catalyses the enzymatic oxidation of insoluble uric acid into highly soluble allantoin, preventing acute uric acid nephropathy.

Hypercalcaemia of malignancy is driven primarily by tumour secretion of parathyroid hormone-related protein PTHrP in over 80% of cases, treated with aggressive isotonic saline and IV zoledronic acid or denosumab.

Malignant spinal cord compression MSCC presents with progressive localized back pain preceding motor weakness; high-dose dexamethasone 10 to 16 mg IV followed by emergent MRI and decompression/radiotherapy is critical.
Superior vena cava syndrome SVC syndrome presents with facial/neck oedema, venous distension, and dyspnea; endovascular stenting provides immediate, durable palliative relief for severe symptoms.

Hyperviscosity syndrome in Waldenstrom macroglobulinemia presents with visual blurring, retinal sausage-link vein segmentation, and mucosal bleeding, managed emergently with therapeutic plasma exchange.

Leukostasis syndrome occurs in acute myeloid leukaemia with blast counts exceeding 100 x 10^9/L, causing pulmonary hypoxia and cerebral microvascular occlusion, managed with emergent hydroxyurea or cytarabine.
Malignant pericardial tamponade presents with Beck triad hypotension, elevated JVP, and muffled heart sounds with pulsus paradoxus, requiring emergency subxiphoid pericardiocentesis.

topics.title: Paraneoplastic syndromes
topics.book: DeVita 12e Ch. 89 (Paraneoplastic Neurologic and Endocrine Syndromes)

mustKnow.fact: Syndrome of inappropriate antidiuretic hormone SIADH presents with euvolemic hyponatremia and concentrated urine caused by ectopic tumour vasopressin, most commonly in small cell lung cancer.
Ectopic ACTH syndrome manifests as rapid-onset hypokalemic metabolic alkalosis, profound proximal myopathy, and severe hypertension, associated with neuroendocrine tumours and small cell lung cancer.

Lambert-Eaton myasthenic syndrome LEMS is driven by autoantibodies against P/Q-type voltage-gated calcium channels VGCC, presenting with proximal leg weakness that paradoxically improves with repetitive muscle use.
Subacute cerebellar degeneration presents with progressive bilateral limb and gait ataxia caused by onconeural antibodies anti-Yo PCA-1 in ovarian/breast cancers or anti-Hu in small cell lung cancer.

Cancer-associated dermatomyositis is marked by heliotrope periorbital rash, Gottron papules on interphalangeal joints, and proximal myopathy, strongly associated with underlying ovarian, lung, and gastrointestinal cancers.
Hypertrophic osteoarthropathy HOA Pierre Marie-Bamberger syndrome comprises digital clubbing, periostitis of distal tubular bones, and symmetrical arthritis secondary to non-small cell lung cancer.
Trousseau syndrome migratory superficial thrombophlebitis represents tumour mucin-driven procoagulant activation, classically heralding occult pancreatic or gastrointestinal adenocarcinomas.
Anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis is characterized by acute psychiatric disturbances, autonomic instability, and seizures in young females, strongly linked to benign or malignant ovarian teratomas.

topics.title: Cancer associated thrombosis
topics.book: DeVita 12e Ch. 97 (Cancer-Associated Venous Thromboembolism)

mustKnow.fact: The Khorana risk score stratifies venous thromboembolism VTE risk in ambulatory cancer patients initiating chemotherapy based on cancer site, platelet, leukocyte, and haemoglobin counts, and BMI.
Low molecular weight heparin LMWH dalteparin proved superior to oral vitamin K antagonists in reducing recurrent VTE without excess bleeding in cancer patients in the CLOT trial.

Direct oral anticoagulants DOACs apixaban, edoxaban, and rivaroxaban are approved first-line alternatives to LMWH for cancer-associated thrombosis in the CARAVAGGIO, Hokusai VTE Cancer, and SELECT-D trials.
Oral DOACs carry an increased risk of gastrointestinal and genitourinary mucosal bleeding compared to LMWH in patients with unresected luminal gastrointestinal or urothelial tumours.

Primary thromboprophylaxis with oral apixaban 2.5 mg twice daily or rivaroxaban 10 mg daily significantly reduces VTE in intermediate-to-high risk outpatients with Khorana score 2 or higher in AVERT and CASSINI.
Central venous catheter-related thrombosis is managed with therapeutic anticoagulation without mandatory catheter removal if the line remains well-positioned, functional, and non-infected.
Incidental asymptomatic pulmonary embolism detected on staging contrast-enhanced CT scans carries clinical outcomes comparable to symptomatic PE, warranting identical therapeutic anticoagulation.
Cancer-associated thrombosis anticoagulation is recommended for a minimum duration of 6 months, continuing indefinitely while active cancer or active anticancer therapy is ongoing.

topics.title: Cancer pain and palliative care
topics.book: DeVita 12e Ch. 98 & 103 (Cancer Pain and Palliative Medicine)

mustKnow.fact: The WHO analgesic ladder guides cancer pain management progressing from non-opioids Step 1, to weak opioids Step 2, up to potent strong opioids Step 3 for moderate-to-severe pain.
Morphine is the reference first-line strong opioid; oral morphine is approximately one-third as potent as parenteral intravenous/subcutaneous morphine due to first-pass metabolism.
Equianalgesic opioid rotation is indicated for refractory neurotoxic adverse effects hyperalgesia, myoclonus, hallucination or poorly responsive pain despite dose escalation.
Neuropathic cancer pain is treated by adding adjuvant co-analgesics gabapentin, pregabalin, duloxetine, or tricyclic antidepressants to baseline opioid regimens.
Breakthrough cancer pain is managed with rapid-onset transmucosal fentanyl formulations or immediate-release oral opioids dosed at approximately 10% to 15% of the total 24-hour baseline opioid dose.

Early integrated palliative care introduced concurrently with standard oncology care within 8 weeks of diagnosis significantly improves quality of life, mood, and overall survival in the landmark Temel trial.
Dame Cicely Saunders total pain concept encompasses physical nociceptive suffering, psychological anxiety, social isolation, and existential/spiritual distress.
mustKnow.source: Cicely Saunders / Oxford Textbook of Palliative Medicine

mustKnow.fact: Palliative proportional sedation utilizing continuous infusion midazolam is ethically indicated for refractory suffering and intractable physical distress in the terminal last days of life.
mustKnow.source: EAPC Recommended Framework on Palliative Sedation

modules.name: Bone metastases and skeletal related events

topics.title: Bone metastases and skeletal related events
topics.book: DeVita 12e Ch. 86 (Metastatic Disease to Bone and Skeletal Complications)

mustKnow.fact: Bone metastases are classified pathophysiologically into osteolytic lesions driven by osteoclast activation in myeloma/breast cancer and osteoblastic lesions in prostate cancer.
Intravenous zoledronic acid 4 mg infused over at least 15 minutes every 3 to 4 weeks significantly reduces skeletal-related events SREs in metastatic bone disease.
Denosumab fully human anti-RANKL monoclonal antibody administered subcutaneously 120 mg every 4 weeks demonstrates superior prevention of SREs compared to zoledronic acid.
mustKnow.source: Fizazi et al. / Stopeck et al. (Lancet)

mustKnow.fact: Medication-related osteonecrosis of the jaw MRONJ is a severe oral complication of antiresorptive therapy; a comprehensive dental evaluation is mandatory prior to initiating bone-modifying agents.

The Mirels scoring system quantifies pathological fracture risk in long bone metastases based on site, size, radiographic appearance, and pain, where a score of 9 or higher indicates prophylactic surgical fixation.
Single-fraction external beam radiotherapy 8 Gy in 1 fraction provides equal pain relief compared to multifraction regimens 30 Gy in 10 fractions for uncomplicated bone metastases.
Radium-223 is an alpha-emitting radiopharmaceutical targeting areas of osteoblastic bone turnover, significantly prolonging overall survival in prostate cancer bone metastases.
Severe hypocalcaemia is a critical complication of denosumab and bisphosphonates; baseline serum calcium and vitamin D levels must be replete and supplemented with daily calcium and calcitriol.

topics.title: Brain and leptomeningeal metastases
topics.book: DeVita 12e Ch. 83 (Metastatic Disease to the Brain and Leptomeninges)

mustKnow.fact: Brain metastases are the most common intracranial tumours in adults, originating primarily from lung cancer 50%, breast cancer 20%, and cutaneous melanoma 10%.

Stereotactic radiosurgery SRS delivers highly focused, ablative radiation doses in a single fraction to 1 to 4 intact brain metastases, preserving neurocognitive function compared to whole-brain radiation.
Whole-brain radiotherapy WBRT with hippocampal avoidance and memantine significantly reduces cognitive decline and executive memory deterioration in multiple brain metastases in NRG CC001.
Third-generation EGFR TKI osimertinib achieves high central nervous system penetration with intracranial response rates reaching 80% in EGFR-mutant NSCLC brain metastases.

Tucatinib HER2-selective TKI combined with trastuzumab and capecitabine significantly reduces CNS disease progression and improves overall survival in HER2-positive breast cancer with brain metastases.
Leptomeningeal carcinomatosis is diagnosed by positive cerebrospinal fluid cytology or linear leptomeningeal enhancement on contrast-enhanced spinal and cranial MRI.
Intrathecal chemotherapy using preservative-free methotrexate, cytarabine, or liposomal cytarabine via an implanted subcutaneous Ommaya reservoir treats leptomeningeal tumour seeding.
Dexamethasone is the primary initial medical therapy for peritumoural vasogenic cerebral oedema, restoring blood-brain barrier integrity and rapidly reversing neurological deficits.

topics.title: Infections in the cancer patient
topics.book: DeVita 12e Ch. 88 (Infectious Complications in Oncology)

mustKnow.fact: Neutropenic fever in cancer patients is an acute medical emergency; blood cultures from both central line lumens and peripheral veins must be drawn prior to immediate empirical broad-spectrum antibiotics within 60 minutes.
Invasive aspergillosis is the leading fungal killer in prolonged neutropenia and stem cell transplantation, presenting with chest CT halo signs and air-crescent signs.
Serum and bronchoalveolar lavage galactomannan antigen detection provides high sensitivity for early diagnosis of invasive aspergillosis before definitive radiographic cavitation occurs.
Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole TMP-SMX prophylaxis is mandatory for patients receiving high-dose corticosteroids, fludarabine, or hyper-CVAD to prevent Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia PJP.
Hepatitis B virus HBV screening with HBsAg and anti-HBc is mandatory prior to rituximab or cytotoxic chemotherapy; entecavir or tenofovir prophylaxis prevents fatal fulminant HBV reactivation.

Cytomegalovirus CMV reactivation is monitored with serial quantitative PCR following allogeneic stem cell transplantation; preemptive therapy with oral valganciclovir or IV ganciclovir prevents tissue-invasive CMV disease.

Mucormycosis zygomycosis is an aggressive, angioinvasive fungal infection in diabetic or neutropenic patients presenting with reverse halo signs and necrotic eschars, treated with emergent debridement and liposomal amphotericin B.

Inactivated vaccines influenza, pneumococcal, recombinant zoster are safe in cancer patients, whereas live-attenuated vaccines MMR, yellow fever, oral polio are strictly contraindicated during immunosuppressive therapy.

topics.title: Malignant effusions, cachexia and nutrition
topics.book: DeVita 12e Ch. 87 & 99 (Malignant Effusions, Cachexia and Nutritional Support)

mustKnow.fact: Malignant pleural effusion MPE causes progressive dyspnea; chemical pleurodesis using sterile talc poudrage or slurry induces robust visceral-parietal pleural symphysis preventing recurrence.
mustKnow.source: ATS / ERS Malignant Pleural Effusion Guidelines

mustKnow.fact: Indwelling pleural catheters IPC provide equivalent symptom control to talc pleurodesis with significantly fewer hospitalisation days, serving as the preferred option for non-expandable trapped lung.

Malignant ascites arises from peritoneal tumour seeding and impaired lymphatic drainage in ovarian, gastrointestinal, and breast cancers, managed with therapeutic paracentesis and intraperitoneal drainage.

Cancer cachexia is a multifactorial metabolic syndrome characterized by involuntary skeletal muscle loss with or without fat wasting, driven by systemic inflammation and catabolic cytokines TNF-alpha and IL-6.
Anamorelin is an oral selective ghrelin receptor agonist that significantly increases appetite, body weight, and lean body mass in advanced non-small cell lung cancer cachexia in the ROMANA trials.
Low-dose olanzapine 2.5 to 5 mg daily significantly stimulates appetite and promotes weight gain in patients with advanced cancer cachexia receiving palliative care.
Malignant bowel obstruction MBO in advanced peritoneal carcinomatosis is managed medically with continuous subcutaneous octreotide somatostatin analogue, antiemetics, and dexamethasone.
Home parenteral nutrition HPN is reserved strictly for aphagic advanced cancer patients with gastrointestinal obstruction who possess an anticipated functional survival exceeding 2 to 3 months.
